proposals.evidence: DEDR946 gives Tamil uṭai/oṭi with past -nt-, Malayalam uṭayuka/oṭiyuka, Kannada oḍe/oḍi and Kodagu oḍand- broken. These survey oḍan-/uḍañ-/oḍend-/voḍa- forms retain that break/broken family with ordinary participial endings and source vowels/voicing. Longer responses with separate go/other auxiliaries are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR958 gives Kannada oṭṭu total/heap and oṭṭaje mass/company, with Tulu oṭṭu the whole. These neighbouring-lect oṭṭukku/oṭṭukka/voṭṭaya/oṭaya all/whole responses are comparative total/union formations in this specific oṭṭu family, preserving their source endings rather than assigning them to the separate numeral parent990. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4572 documents the southern pō-/pōk-/ōg- go family, including Malayalam pōka, Kannada pōgu/hōgu/ōgu and Kota ōg-. These survey pō/ōgu/vōgu/pīge responses compare with that go family and retain source vowels and ordinary endings; no longer auxiliary phrase is included. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3098 explicitly gives Tamil/Malayalam tā(r)- give with tā imperative and the same first/second-person giving meaning in Badaga. Betta Kurumba tara and Irula tā give are comparative continuations of that giving stem; retain the elicited general give gloss without inventing a specified recipient. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
